title: Your First Apartment Costs More Than the Rent
summary: Eli and Rosa are both 20 and both earn $18.50 an hour. Eli's studio rents for $1,150, but getting the keys takes about $3,100, and his real monthly housing bill eats about half his take-home pay. This video covers seven moves for your first apartment: the 30% rule, the landlord's 3x income test, the real monthly bill, move-in cash, renters insurance, roommate math, and what to read in the lease, plus an honest look at where the 30% rule breaks down. Examples assume $2,600 take-home pay a month, $110 utilities, $60 internet, $14 renters insurance, a one-month deposit, $50 application fee and a 5% renewal increase; they are illustrations, not quotes for your city. Eli and Rosa are fictional composites.
